name: The Hague
tagline: The genuine seat of Dutch government and international justice, its stately art museums and North Sea beach giving it a character quite different from Amsterdam's tourist bustle.
highlight: Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring at the Mauritshuis, a small painting that draws a disproportionate crowd of admirers to a quiet corner of one room.
shortDescription: The Netherlands' seat of government and international law, its Mauritshuis art collection and Scheveningen beach giving it a different pace from Amsterdam.
metaDescription: A The Hague travel guide: the Mauritshuis, the Binnenhof, Scheveningen beach, Dutch food, when to go and a practical two-day itinerary.
nearestAirport: Rotterdam The Hague Airport (RTM), or Amsterdam Schiphol (AMS)
knownFor: The Mauritshuis, the Binnenhof, Scheveningen beach
goodFor: Art, government history, an easy beach afternoon

image.alt: The Mauritshuis art museum on the Hofvijver lake in The Hague

intro: The Hague has been the seat of Dutch government since the 13th century, and despite that, it has never been the country's official capital — Amsterdam holds that title constitutionally, while The Hague runs the country day to day, hosting parliament, the royal family's working palace, and the International Court of Justice.

That institutional weight gives the city a different character from Amsterdam: stately rather than bustling, with the compact Mauritshuis holding one of the finest small art collections in Europe, anchored by Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring and Rembrandt's The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp.

The Hague is also, unusually for a European seat of government, a beach town — Scheveningen, its North Sea resort district, sits just a tram ride from the government quarter, giving visitors a legitimate reason to combine museum-going with a walk along the pier.

whyVisit.intro: The Hague's case is a world-class small art collection paired with real government and international-law history, plus a North Sea beach few European capitals can offer.

points.title: The Mauritshuis is one of Europe's finest small museums
points.text: A compact collection built almost entirely of masterpieces, including Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring, without the overwhelming scale of a larger institution.

points.title: It's the working seat of Dutch government
points.text: The Binnenhof complex has housed Dutch political power since the 13th century and remains in active use today.

points.title: It's home to international justice
points.text: The Peace Palace houses the International Court of Justice, giving The Hague a real global significance beyond its size.

points.title: Scheveningen adds a genuine beach dimension
points.text: A proper North Sea resort with a pier and boardwalk, a short tram ride from the museums and government quarter.

points.title: It's less crowded than Amsterdam
points.text: The Hague's sights rarely feel overrun, even at the Mauritshuis, despite the quality of what's on show.

attractionsIntro: The Hague's essential sights span its government quarter, world-class small museums and North Sea coastline.

attractions.name: The Mauritshuis

image.alt: The Mauritshuis art museum on the Hofvijver lake in The Hague

attractions.text: A compact 17th-century townhouse turned museum, its collection built almost entirely of masterpieces — Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring, Rembrandt's The Anatomy Lesson, and Carel Fabritius's The Goldfinch among them.
attractions.tip: Book timed-entry tickets online — the collection's small scale means the museum limits visitor numbers even outside peak season.

attractions.name: The Binnenhof

image.alt: The historic Binnenhof government complex in The Hague

attractions.text: The genuine seat of Dutch political power since the 13th century, its medieval Ridderzaal (Hall of Knights) still used for the annual state opening of parliament.
attractions.tip: The complex reopened after major renovation — check current visitor access, since parts function as working government offices.

attractions.name: The Peace Palace

image.file: File:Den Haag, het Vredespaleis RM333074 IMG 4317 2024-08-05 10.02.jpg
image.alt: The Peace Palace, home to the International Court of Justice, in The Hague

attractions.text: A grand 1913 building housing the International Court of Justice and the Permanent Court of Arbitration, giving The Hague real standing as a centre of international law.
attractions.tip: The visitor centre across the road explains the building's role even when court sessions aren't open to the public.

attractions.name: Madurodam

image.alt: Miniature-scale Dutch buildings and landmarks at Madurodam

attractions.text: A charming miniature park recreating the Netherlands' most famous buildings and landmarks at 1:25 scale, a national institution since 1952.
attractions.tip: Best suited to visitors travelling with children, though the detail and craftsmanship have a real appeal regardless of age.

attractions.name: Scheveningen Pier

image.alt: Scheveningen Pier extending into the North Sea at The Hague's beach district

attractions.text: A long pier extending out over the North Sea, with a Ferris wheel, bungee jump and a long sandy beach stretching in both directions below the boardwalk.
attractions.tip: The pier and boardwalk are a short, direct tram ride from the museums and government quarter — easy to combine in one day.

attractions.name: Panorama Mesdag

image.alt: The vast 19th-century cylindrical seascape painting Panorama Mesdag

attractions.text: An enormous 1881 cylindrical painting of the Scheveningen coast, viewed from a central platform designed to create a full 360-degree illusion of standing on the dunes.
attractions.tip: One of the world's oldest surviving panorama paintings still displayed in its purpose-built rotunda — worth the modest entry fee.

attractions.name: Escher in Het Paleis

image.file: File:Gevel Escher in Het Paleis 300 dpi.jpg
image.alt: The former royal palace now housing the Escher in Het Paleis museum in The Hague

attractions.text: A former royal winter palace now dedicated to M.C. Escher's mind-bending graphic work, the optical-illusion prints displayed in a fittingly grand historic setting.
attractions.tip: The top floor's illusion rooms are popular for photos — expect a short wait during busy periods.

thingsToDoIntro: Beyond the museums and government quarter, The Hague rewards its North Sea coastline and a genuine day-trip case for nearby Delft.

thingsToDo.title: Walk Scheveningen's beach and pier

image.file: File:People at Scheveningen Beach in The Hague (2015-08-13).jpg
image.alt: The sandy beach at Scheveningen, The Hague's North Sea resort district

thingsToDo.text: A proper North Sea beach and boardwalk, a short tram ride from the museums, with beach clubs, a pier and a long stretch of sand in both directions.
thingsToDo.tip: Sunset here is worth timing a visit around — the pier and boardwalk face directly into the evening light.

thingsToDo.title: See Girl with a Pearl Earring up close

image.alt: A gallery room inside the Mauritshuis museum in The Hague

thingsToDo.text: Vermeer's small, famous portrait draws a disproportionate crowd to one quiet corner of the Mauritshuis — worth timing your visit for a moment when the room is less busy.
thingsToDo.tip: Early morning, right at opening, gives the best chance of a quieter moment in front of the painting.

thingsToDo.title: Cycle the North Sea coast dunes
thingsToDo.text: Dedicated cycle paths run along the dunes north and south of Scheveningen, offering a completely different, wilder coastal landscape than the beach town itself.
thingsToDo.tip: The dunes north toward Wassenaar are quieter and less developed than the stretch immediately by the pier.

thingsToDo.title: Explore the Hofvijver and government quarter

image.alt: The Hofvijver lake reflecting the Binnenhof government buildings in The Hague

thingsToDo.text: The reflecting lake beside the Binnenhof gives one of the most photographed views in the city, the government buildings mirrored in still water.
thingsToDo.tip: The Lange Voorhout street nearby, lined with grand townhouses, is a pleasant extension of the same walk.

thingsToDo.title: Day-trip to Delft

image.alt: A canal in the historic centre of Delft, near The Hague

thingsToDo.text: Vermeer's home city is just a short tram ride away, its old town and Delftware tradition making an easy half-day addition to a Hague stay.
thingsToDo.tip: Tram 1 runs directly between The Hague and Delft's centre — no train transfer required.

thingsToDo.title: Browse the Grote Markt

image.alt: The Grote Markt square in central The Hague

thingsToDo.text: The city's central square, lively with restaurant terraces and a lower-key, more local feel than the museum quarter nearby.
thingsToDo.tip: A good spot for an evening meal after a day of museums — more relaxed than the tourist-heavy streets near the Mauritshuis.

foodIntro: The Hague's food culture carries a strong Indonesian-Dutch heritage alongside the usual Dutch classics, a legacy of returnees from the former Dutch East Indies.

foods.name: Stroopwafel

image.alt: Stroopwafels, thin waffles filled with caramel syrup

foods.text: Two thin waffles sandwiching a gooey caramel syrup filling, best bought fresh and warm rather than a packaged supermarket version.
foods.whereToTry: Market stalls around the Grote Markt and city centre.

foods.name: Bitterballen

image.file: File:Bitterballen with Dijon mustard - Taproom ‘t Blauwe Theehuis 2024-11-26.jpg
image.alt: A plate of bitterballen, deep-fried Dutch meat croquettes, with mustard

foods.text: Deep-fried, breadcrumbed balls of a rich beef ragout, the classic accompaniment to a beer at any Dutch bar.
foods.whereToTry: Bars around the Grote Markt and Plein squares.

foods.name: Haring (raw herring)

image.alt: Raw Dutch herring served with chopped onion

foods.text: Lightly cured raw herring, traditionally eaten by the tail with chopped onion — a genuine Dutch institution, especially good fresh near the Scheveningen fishing harbour.
foods.whereToTry: Herring stalls around Scheveningen's harbour and the city centre markets.

foods.name: Rijsttafel on Javastraat

image.alt: A rijsttafel spread of Indonesian dishes served on The Hague's Javastraat

foods.text: An elaborate spread of small Indonesian dishes, a defining Hague tradition thanks to a large community with roots in the former Dutch East Indies, concentrated along Javastraat.
foods.whereToTry: Long-running Indonesian restaurants on and around Javastraat, several open for generations.

foods.name: Kibbeling

image.alt: A portion of kibbeling, Dutch battered fried fish, with sauce

foods.text: Bite-sized battered, deep-fried white fish with a garlicky sauce, at its best fresh from a stall near Scheveningen's fishing harbour.
foods.whereToTry: Fish stalls along the Scheveningen harbourfront.

foods.name: Haagse hopjes

image.alt: Haagse hopjes, coffee-flavoured caramel sweets from The Hague

foods.text: Small coffee-flavoured caramel sweets invented in The Hague in the 18th century, still sold in the distinctive tins found in shops across the city.
foods.whereToTry: Confectioners and souvenir shops throughout the city centre.

accommodation.intro: The Hague splits between the stately city centre and the beach at Scheveningen, both easy bases.

areas.name: City centre
areas.bestFor: Walking distance to the Mauritshuis and Binnenhof
areas.text: The government and museum quarter, the most convenient base for sightseeing, with a mix of business and boutique hotels.

areas.name: Scheveningen
areas.bestFor: A beach-town stay with easy tram access to the centre
areas.text: More resort-like than the city centre, with sea-view hotels and a short, direct tram ride to the museums.

gettingThere.intro: The Hague sits on the main rail line through the Randstad, easy to reach from anywhere in the region.

options.text: Direct intercity trains connect [[amsterdam|Amsterdam]] to The Hague in under an hour.
options.detail: Trains arrive at either Den Haag Centraal or Den Haag HS — check which is closer to your accommodation.

options.text: Both [[rotterdam|Rotterdam]] and [[delft|Delft]] connect to The Hague in well under 30 minutes.
options.detail: Tram 1 also runs directly to Delft, a scenic alternative to the train.

options.text: A smaller regional airport with limited European routes; Amsterdam Schiphol is the main international gateway.
options.detail: A direct train or bus connects the airport area to The Hague's centre.

gettingAround.intro: The Hague's centre is walkable, with trams reaching Scheveningen and the outer neighbourhoods easily.

options.text: The Mauritshuis, Binnenhof and Hofvijver are all within a compact, walkable government and museum quarter.
options.detail: The city centre is flat and easy to cover on foot in a morning.

options.text: A comprehensive network connects the centre to Scheveningen, Madurodam and the wider city efficiently.
options.detail: An OV-chipkaart or contactless card covers all HTM transit — tap in and out on every journey.

options.text: Flat terrain and good cycle paths make biking a pleasant way to reach Scheveningen or the dunes.
options.detail: Rental is available near both main train stations and throughout the city centre.

bestTime.headline: May–September for the beach, or any season for the museums
bestTime.summary: The Hague's museums work year-round, but Scheveningen's beach only comes alive in the warmer months.

seasons.text: Mild temperatures and thinning crowds, with the beach starting to come back to life by May.
The best weather for Scheveningen's beach and boardwalk, alongside the museums' full opening hours.
Mild and quiet, a good season for the museums without summer's beach crowds.
Cold, grey and often windy on the coast, though the Mauritshuis and other indoor sights work well regardless.

bestTime.avoid: Nothing strongly — the museums are a year-round draw regardless of beach weather.

itinerary.title: Two days in The Hague
itinerary.intro: Built around the museum quarter, with the beach and a Delft day trip rounding out the visit.

days.title: Museums and government quarter
days.summary: The city's essential art and history.
days.afternoon: The Binnenhof, Hofvijver and Lange Voorhout.

days.title: The coast, or a Delft day trip
days.summary: Either the beach or a short trip to Vermeer's home city.
days.morning: Scheveningen's pier and beach, or the tram to Delft.
days.afternoon: Madurodam or Panorama Mesdag, or continued exploring in Delft.

tipsIntro: Practical notes on booking, timing and transport that make a real difference to a The Hague trip.
tips: Book Mauritshuis tickets online ahead — the museum's small scale means it limits visitor numbers even outside peak season.
Check which station your train arrives at — Den Haag Centraal or Den Haag HS — before booking accommodation.
Combine The Hague with Delft via Tram 1 rather than the train — it's a scenic, direct alternative.
Time a Scheveningen visit for late afternoon and sunset — the pier and boardwalk face directly into the evening light.
Carry a contactless card — many smaller vendors no longer accept cash at all.
Book a rijsttafel dinner on Javastraat ahead on weekends — the best-known restaurants fill up.

faq.q: Is The Hague worth visiting alongside Amsterdam?
faq.a: Yes — it offers world-class small museums, real government and international-law history, and a proper North Sea beach, all in under an hour from Amsterdam by train.

faq.q: How many days do you need in The Hague?
faq.a: One to two days covers the Mauritshuis, Binnenhof and Scheveningen beach comfortably. A day trip from Amsterdam is workable but rushed given the quality of the museums.

faq.q: Is The Hague the capital of the Netherlands?
faq.a: No — Amsterdam holds that title constitutionally, but The Hague is the genuine seat of government, hosting parliament, the working royal palace and the International Court of Justice.

faq.q: What is the Mauritshuis known for?
faq.a: A compact 17th-century collection built almost entirely of masterpieces, most famously Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring, alongside major works by Rembrandt and other Dutch Golden Age painters.

faq.q: Can you combine The Hague with a beach day?
faq.a: Yes, easily — Scheveningen, The Hague's North Sea resort district, is a short direct tram ride from the museum and government quarter.

faq.q: Is Delft easy to visit from The Hague?
faq.a: Yes, very — Tram 1 runs directly between the two, taking well under 30 minutes, making Delft an easy half-day addition to a Hague stay.
